lines.text: The Netherlands lies in Europe.
The neighboring countries [buurlanden] are Germany and Belgium.
In the east the Netherlands borders [grenst] Germany, in the south Belgium.
The Netherlands has about 18 million inhabitants [18 miljoen inwoners].
The Netherlands has twelve provinces [twaalf provincies].
Each province has a capital:
The province of Groningen has Groningen as its capital.
The province of Friesland has Leeuwarden as its capital.
The province of Drenthe has Assen as its capital.
The province of Overijssel has Zwolle as its capital.
The province of Flevoland has Lelystad as its capital.
The province of Gelderland has Arnhem as its capital.
The province of Utrecht has Utrecht as its capital.
The province of Noord-Holland has Haarlem as its capital.
The province of Zuid-Holland has Den Haag as its capital.
The province of Zeeland has Middelburg as its capital.
The province of Noord-Brabant has 's-Hertogenbosch as its capital.
The province of Limburg has Maastricht as its capital.
The four largest cities lie in the west.
That area is called de Randstad.
It is busy there; many people live there.
Amsterdam is the capital [hoofdstad] and the largest city.
Rotterdam is the second city, with the largest port [haven] in Europe.
Den Haag is the third city.
The government [regering] is not in Amsterdam, but in Den Haag.
Utrecht is the fourth city and lies in the middle of the Netherlands.
The Netherlands belongs to the European Union [Europese Unie (EU)]: countries in Europe that work together.
Residents of the EU may live, work or study [studeren] in other EU countries.
They may travel freely, so they do not need a visa [visum] within the EU.
They may also buy goods in other countries and bring them to the Netherlands.
The EU countries make agreements, for example about money: since 2002 people in many countries pay with the euro.
There are also agreements about the environment [milieu] and about taking in [opvangen] refugees [vluchtelingen].
The European Parliament [Europees Parlement] decides on rules and agreements within the EU.
The Netherlands must keep to those agreements and cannot simply say: we no longer want to take in refugees.
